title: 月河桥 Yuehe Qiao
subtitle: Yuanming Yuan

model.line: The ancestral temple 安佑宫 as S01 draws its layout and S05 names its halls (1742-43, after 寿皇殿): the hall of nine bays on S01's grid of ten by four columns (Malone counted forty pillars), double-eaved 歇山 in yellow tile after the leaf of 1744, on its marble terrace with five flights; the gate 安佑门, the two walls, the two moats with five bridges each, the three timber archways, the glazed archway and the four 华表 as S01, S05, Malone and the leaf give them. Every height, the smaller buildings' forms and all ornament are C.
rows: Layout

As S01 draws it (re-read in Round 27 in plan pixels, B): from the four 华表 round the glazed archway in the south, past 致孚殿, over the outer moat to the forecourt, the outer wall, the court between the walls with the inner moat, 安佑门 in the inner wall and the inner court with the hall at its back; one axis through them
安佑宫

Nine bays (S05 重檐正殿九楹, A) on S01's ten column lines and four rows, about 30 x 14 m between the end columns (B; Malone counted ten pillars across the front and forty in all, B); a porch at the front, red lattice doors in every bay, red columns, green-blue beams under both eaves (the leaf, A); double-eaved 歇山 in yellow glazed tile (the leaf, A; S360, Malone, B); the plaque 安佑宫 in Qianlong's hand (S05, A); the column 4.6 m from the leaf's proportion, the roofs' rise C
Terrace

One marble terrace under the hall and before it, T-shaped as S01 draws it, with five flights, three at the front and one on each side of the 月台 (S01; Malone's five stairs, B); the middle flight with the dragon-and-cloud ramp stone, 1.30 m wide (S943: one of its stones is at Peking University, B); white balustrades (the leaf, A); its height 1.6 m C; two censers, two cranes and two deer before the hall (S361, Malone, B; their forms and places C)
Inner court

The side halls 配殿 of five bays, yellow 歇山 (S05, A; the leaf; S01), the two octagonal stele pavilions with double eaves (S05, Malone, the leaf; S01's octagons), the two green-glazed burners (S05, Malone, B; form C); a way on the axis (C); the court's trees are the planting's (the leaf's rows of small conifers)
安佑门

Five bays (S05, A), single-eave 歇山 in yellow tile (the leaf, A), its doors in the middle row on the inner wall's line (S01, B), on a marble terrace with a balustrade and three flights (Malone, the leaf, B; its size C); the plaque 安佑门 (S05, A)
Walls

Two red walls with yellow glazed coping (Malone, B; the leaf paints them vermilion), 72 x 61 m and 96 x 100 m as S01 draws them (B); a small gate either side of 安佑门 (S01; the leaf); the outer wall's five gates: three glazed arched gates in the middle and a smaller gate each side (Malone, S01, the leaf; B), a gate of three bays on the north side (S01); heights C
Between the walls

The inner moat, a moon river with three marble bridges before the gate and one at each side (S05, A; Malone, B; S01's channel and breaks: water of Round 27), its lining and railings C; the waiting rooms 朝房 of five bays (S05, A; form C); two well pavilions (S05, Malone; form C); in the north corners two walled yards with long ranges (S01; unnamed, C)
Forecourt

The two stone qilin on their bases before the three middle gates (Malone; S943: 1.74 m on bases 0.98 m high, 1.41 x 1.95 m; S01's squares; B; the beast's form C); the three timber archways 三坊 with red posts held by diagonal props and small yellow roofs (S05, A, with their six faces named; the leaf, A; S01's bars), their heights C; paved (the leaf)
Outer moat

The U-shaped moat 月河 round the forecourt (S05, A; S01's band: water of Round 27) with five marble bridges, the middle one for the emperor (Malone, B); three arched bridges with white balustrades and red railings along the banks as the leaf paints them (A); the two end bridges and the lining C
致孚殿
Three bays facing west in a red-walled yard, yellow tile (S05, A; the leaf, A; S01's yard and cells, B); inside, the carved text of Yongzheng's 圆明园记 (S05 j81:21b; not drawn); heights C
Glazed archway and 华表

鸿慈永祜坊 (S05, A): three gates with glazed frames and yellow roofs between four short red walls with round glazed panels (Malone, B; the leaf, A), 13.7 m as S01 draws it (B), its heights C; the four marble 华表 at the corners of a square of 30 m (Malone, S01: B), 8 m high on octagonal bases 1.24 m high (S980, B), the dragon, cloud board, dew plate and beast after the photograph of about 1882 (P0196) and the pair at Peking University (C for their sizes)
What survives

The 华表: two at Peking University, two before the old National Library (moved 1925; S980); the qilin pair at Peking University (S943); one ramp stone at Peking University, its pair at the east gate of 颐和园 (S943). The masonry was pulled down under the Republic (S02 p.218); no dig of the platform has been published
Assumed

Every height (the terrace 1.6 m, the hall's column 4.6 m and its roofs, the gates', walls', archways' and pavilions' heights), the porches, the brackets, the corner ranges, the waiting rooms', wells' and burners' forms, the bronzes, the qilin's and 华表's carving, the bridges' form, the linings and railings: the classes, the Qing manual and the leaf (C, the pale tint with conf=1)

evidence.title: 日下舊聞考 鸿慈永祜
evidence.excerpt_zh: 月地雲居之後循山徑入為鴻慈永祜安佑宫前琉璃坊座南面額也左右石華表各一坊南及東西復有三坊環列其南為月河橋又東南為致孚殿三楹西向宫門五楹南向為安佑門門前白玉石橋三座左右井亭各一朝房各五楹門内重檐正殿九楹為安佑宫殿内中龕敬奉聖祖仁皇帝聖容左龕敬奉世宗憲皇帝聖容左右配殿各五楹碑亭各一燎亭各一（圓明園冊）臣等謹按安佑宫建自乾隆七年皇上恭仿夀皇殿之制敬奉聖祖世宗聖容嵗時朔望瞻禮于兹鴻慈永祜為四十景之一坊北面額曰燕翼長詒鴻慈永祜之前三坊南曰羮牆愾慕曰雲日瞻依東曰勲華式煥曰謨烈重光西曰德配清寧曰功隆作述殿内中龕額曰音容儼在左龕額曰陟降在兹與安佑門安佑宫額皆御書致孚殿内恭刋乾隆七年御筆敬錄世宗圓明園記並御製圓明園後記記文已恭載前卷内
evidence.summary: The imperial ancestral precinct. Glazed archways with named faces, two stone columns and a 月河橋, the three-bay 致孚殿, the five-bay 安佑門 with three marble bridges, well pavilions and court rooms; inside, the double-eaved nine-bay 安佑宫 with portraits of Kangxi and Yongzheng, five-bay side halls, stele and burner pavilions. Built 乾隆七年 (1742) after 壽皇殿.

evidence.title: 鸿慈永祜: moat, gates and the two walls
evidence.excerpt_other: The moat is crossed by five marble bridges, the center one of which is intended for the Emperor alone. Beyond the bridges three pailous form a kind of screen before the gates in the outer wall of the shrine, and the stone figures of two ch'i lin guard the three middle gates
evidence.summary: From the pillars the path passes a small sacrifice building to five marble bridges, three pailou, two stone qilin, five gates in a red wall with yellow glazed coping. Between outer and inner red walls: waiting rooms, a second moat with three bridges and two side bridges, two covered wells, and a marble terrace with the inner gate.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum, Historical Photographs of China, the Rijksmuseum, Wellcome and in NDL's albums of about 1900; today's photographs on Commons.
